# Data card: LSTMABAR dataset v1

<!-- Generated by `lstmabar data freeze` (src/lstmabar/data/card.py). Edit the template in
card.py, not this file: numbers come from data/manifests/<version>/index.json. -->

**Not frozen yet.** Numbers below are filled in by the freeze.

## What it is

Pairs of a clean DI guitar clip and a wet render of it through a physically grounded pedal
(white-box circuit sims for `render.whitebox_pedals`, the grey-box pedalboard for the other pedals and
for free-board settings), each with its parameter labels, measured descriptors, a harmonic
archetype readout, and text captions (template + LLM paraphrase). It trains and evaluates
text-driven tone transformation (design §5). Audio is never committed: the repository holds
code, manifests, hashes and this card. Hashes identify the frozen dataset; re-renders on
another machine need not be bit-identical (CPU float differences).

*Pending: generated by `lstmabar data freeze` once dataset v1 is rendered.*

## Splits

- `train`: the train performers' recordings, minus the val slice.
- `val`: an in-domain **by-recording** slice of the train performers (R11). Val shares
  performers with train, so it measures new recordings, **not new players**.
- `test`: every clip of the held-out performer (Guitar-TECHS `ingest.heldout_performer`) and any own DI. It is
  the only performer-disjoint split (checked at freeze). It is small, and `ingest.heldout_performer` recorded
  only musical excerpts, so test is also **out of domain** in content.
- `test_unseen_pedal`: renders of the holdout pedal on `test` clips only. The holdout pedal
  is never rendered for train or val, and no caption outside this split names it.
- No source recording appears in two splits (checked at freeze).

*Pending: generated by `lstmabar data freeze` once dataset v1 is rendered.*

## Levels (R3)

Dry clips are stored peak-normalized to `ingest.dry_peak_dbfs` (`ingest.dry_subtype`) FLAC with the source gain recorded.
Each render samples its input peak uniformly in `render.input_peak_dbfs` and scales the dry clip to it
before the pedal (0 dBFS = `physics.volts_per_full_scale` peak). Wet renders are stored peak-normalized to `render.wet_peak_dbfs` (`render.wet_subtype`)
FLAC; true wet = file × 10^(`wet_gain_db`/20). At inference, inputs are peak-normalized to
`audio.inference_peak_dbfs`.

*Pending: generated by `lstmabar data freeze` once dataset v1 is rendered.*

## Labels

- `board_params` (normalized knobs + `enabled` gates per block) is the training label.
  Grey-box pedals: `derive()` (`label_source = derived`). White-box pedals: the per-pedal
  calibration table (R4), interpolated (`calibrated`) or the nearest grid point where
  neighbouring fits jump (`calibrated_nearest`); the derived label is kept in
  `board_params_derived` for comparison. Free board: the sampled parameters (`free`).
- `pedal_knobs` holds the pedal-space label (knob rotations in [0, 1]).
- **Clamping (R6, decision 10):** `clamped` flags items whose *derived* label hit Drive's
  60 dB gain limit. Grey-box pedals sound identical above the limit (the clamped label
  is what was rendered); for white-box pedals the audio still differs and only the derived
  label is clamped. Clamped items are kept and flagged so training can down-weight or dedupe
  them. `label_clamp_notes` records clamps in the calibrated label (e.g. the level knob's
  analytic offset).
- **Disabled blocks carry random knob values.** A block with `enabled = 0` still has knob
  numbers in `board_params`; they have no effect on the audio. Mask knob losses and metrics
  by `enabled`.

*Pending: generated by `lstmabar data freeze` once dataset v1 is rendered.*

## Captions (R1, decisions 5–6)

Each item has template captions (deterministic, built from parameters, binned measured
descriptors and KB vocabulary) and LLM paraphrases of them (Message Batches API). A
paraphrase that fails the post-filter is dropped and the item keeps only its template
caption. Captions contain no numbers, units or knob values, name the item's pedal in only a
fraction of pedal items (and only by allowed aliases), and never name the holdout pedal
outside `test_unseen_pedal`; the freeze re-checks every caption with the same rule
(`vocab.item_caption_violations`). The caption code was written **gold-blind**: it never read
the held-out instruction set (`tests/data/test_caption_hygiene.py`). The one-shot vocabulary
overlap audit against that set (`reports/vocab_overlap.md`) runs after freeze; templates are
not changed after seeing it (if they are, the dataset becomes v1.1, "tuned after gold
audit").

*Pending: generated by `lstmabar data freeze` once dataset v1 is rendered.*

## Known limitations

- **60 dB Drive clamp** (P2 finding): derived gain exceeds the limit for DS-1 above
  about a quarter Dist, Big Muff above about half Sustain, Fuzz Face Si at full and RAT at
  max. Grey-box renders of those settings sound identical; white-box renders (here
  `render.whitebox_pedals`) still differ and only their derived label is clamped. Holdout pedal:
  `render.holdout_pedal` (rendered only in `test_unseen_pedal`). Counts are in Labels above.
- **Fuzz Face source impedance**: renders inherit the fixed guitar source impedance assumed
  by the derivation (`physics.source_ohms`).
- **`test_real` sample rate**: EGFxSet and pOD-set audio is stored at its native rate
  (see the `test_real` table); resample before comparing with the `audio.sample_rate` renders. Its
  recordings are level-normalized, so the true pedal input voltage is unknown.
- **EGFxSet pairing**: each effected note is paired with the `Clean` note of the same
  pickup/string/fret, assuming they are the same take; not verified sample-by-sample.
- **EGFxSet license**: CC BY on Zenodo vs CC BY-SA in mirdata (see above).
- **Analysis resolution**: harmonic analysis uses a reduced `analysis.max_frames` (R8
  throughput gate), so harmonic descriptors are estimates from a frame subset; below
  `analysis.min_voiced_fraction` they are not measured (`null`) and captions do not use them.
- **Source levels differ per performer**: see the source-gain and clip-RMS distributions
  below; quiet takes were raised more before peak normalization (more relative noise).
- Val is not performer-disjoint, and test is small and out of domain (see Splits).
